chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who is given wealth to distribute among those whom it is permissible for him to give to: Is it permissible for him to take something from it for himself, even if it has not been specified for him? He (peace be upon him) said: He may take for himself an amount equal to what he gives to others.
ai.seo_question: Can a person entrusted with distributing charity or wealth take a portion for themselves if not specified?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith clarifies the permissibility of a distributor retaining a portion of entrusted funds when no specific share is designated for him. It establishes the principle of equality, ruling that he may take for himself an amount equal to what he distributes to others, reflecting the Shia juristic view on fair compensation in agency (*wakalah*) and distribution contexts.
